gate: C reference corpus (SPRINT-20, re-pinned SPRINT-21 for the .h routing treatment): Debian curl 7.88.1 orig tarball, 799 .c/.h files (+1 cpp pack file, +4 python pack files)

2_parse_honesty.boundary_note: 203/804 analyzed files carry at least one raw-source parse error (pinned): preprocessor-interleaved expressions and control flow, extern "C" guards closed inside #ifdef __cplusplus, GNU named-variadic macros, comment token pasting; the SPRINT-21 routing delta routes 232 inconclusive headers to the cpp grammar (fewer error nodes on the same files). No canonical C corpus parses 100% clean as-written (zlib 46/53, musl 382/2248, sqlite tree 230/436); the pinned count IS the kill-switch -- a grammar or tool regression moves it.

5_rule_honesty.note: OC003=4: REAL include cycles between curl headers (measured, not fabricated). OC005 is empty by construction: every file with in-degree > 0 has its exports marked used by the whole-file include binds. OC011=27: credential-shaped text in curl's test data and docs -- the line-based scan over source as written. No manifest tier exists for C: the supply block is absent and the meta says so.
